name: TONGA

flag.title: Tonga
flag.note: Red field, white canton with red cross

lead: Tonga is the only Pacific island kingdom never colonised by a foreign power — it kept its royal family and pride. Scattered across a vast ocean, its 170 islands hide coral reefs, humpback whale nurseries, and ancient stone arches built by a civilisation that left no writing, only huge rocks fitted perfectly together.
geo: Tonga's 170 islands stretch 800 km north to south. The western chain is volcanic — Kao and Tofua rise steeply from deep ocean. The eastern islands are flat coral limestone, barely above sea level, fringed by colourful reefs.

The Tonga Trench plunges 10,800 metres nearby — one of Earth's deepest points. Every year the islands nudge westward as the Pacific plate slides underneath, making Tonga one of the world's most earthquake-prone places.
animals: Humpback whales swim to Tonga's warm waters every July–October to give birth and sing. You can snorkel right beside them — one of very few places on Earth where that is legal and safe.
The flying fox (fruit bat) is Tonga's largest native land mammal and is considered sacred — only the king may hunt it. Brilliant parrotfish and sea turtles also call these reef waters home.
culture: Tongan society runs on strict rank — chiefs above commoners, and everyone knows their place at a feast. No gathering is complete without a massive umu (underground oven) heaped with pig, yam, and coconut cream.

Women weave fine mats from pandanus leaves that can take years to finish and are more valuable than money at weddings. Tapa cloth — beaten from mulberry bark into big decorated sheets — is given as a royal gift.
history: Tonga's Tu'i Tonga dynasty began around 950 AD, one of the Pacific's oldest royal lines. At its height it controlled trade across Fiji, Samoa, and Niue — a Pacific superpower run from a coral island.

Captain Cook visited three times and called it the 'Friendly Islands'. King Tāufa'āhau Tupou I wrote a constitution in 1875 before Britain could take full control. Tonga joined the Commonwealth in 1970 as the only monarchy.
wows: Tonga is the only Pacific nation never formally colonised by a European power.
You can legally swim alongside humpback whale mothers and newborn calves in Tonga.
Tonga sits so far east it is often the first country to ring in the New Year.
The Ha'amonga 'a Maui is a 40-tonne coral arch built c.1200 AD — Tonga's Stonehenge.
Flying foxes in Tonga are royal property; commoners are banned from hunting them.
Tonga's rugby team has beaten France and Italy at Rugby World Cups.
Tongans rank among the tallest and heaviest people on Earth on average.

myths.fact: Tonga is 170 islands spread across an ocean area bigger than France, though total dry land is tiny.

myths.myth: All Pacific islands are the same
myths.fact: Tonga has its own royal culture, ranked society, and unique language — and was never colonised, unlike most neighbours.
